prompt: A wavetable serves a range of pitches. At which pitch should you set its strict below-Nyquist source-harmonic limit?

options.text: The highest pitch served by that table
options.explanation: Correct. That is where each retained harmonic reaches its highest frequency and has the least room below Nyquist.

options.text: The lowest pitch, because low notes contain more harmonics
options.explanation: A table built only for the lowest pitch can carry unsafe harmonics when played higher.

options.text: Any pitch: storing samples automatically prevents aliasing
options.explanation: Stored cycles do not automatically constrain playback spectrum; interpolation also needs checking.

options.text: Only the middle pitch, ignoring the endpoints
options.explanation: The upper endpoint can violate the limit even if the middle is safe.

workedExample: As playback pitch rises, every table harmonic rises by the same ratio. Choose source harmonics for the highest pitch in the range, then inspect playback interpolation and modulation separately. Lower notes in that range may be less bright than their own bandwidth would allow.

prompt: You generate saws by summing every harmonic below Nyquist separately for every voice. Which workload is likely to be most demanding at a fixed sample rate?

options.explanation: Correct. Low notes fit more harmonics, and independent voices multiply that work.

options.text: One high note, because its fundamental is higher
options.explanation: A high fundamental leaves room for fewer below-Nyquist harmonics.

options.text: Any note count, because the harmonic sum is computed only at note-on
options.explanation: In this stated implementation the sine components must be evaluated throughout playback.

options.text: An idle voice pool, because unused voices contain more harmonics
options.explanation: Idle voices need not perform the active per-harmonic work.

workedExample: Count the causes of work qualitatively: lower pitch permits more components, and polyphony repeats the calculation for more voices. Tables built offline move that harmonic construction out of playback, trading memory for playback cost. Measure the actual target before selecting a voice limit.

prompt: A table design intentionally permits aliases confined near the top of the output band to retain more brightness. Which description is honest?

options.text: It is strictly alias-free because many listeners cannot hear the top band
options.explanation: An audibility assumption does not change whether folding occurs.

options.text: It uses an explicit spectral-error tolerance that must be checked across its pitch range and processing chain
options.explanation: Correct. The aliases remain; their audibility and later interactions depend on the application.

options.text: It is safe for arbitrary pitch modulation once one static top note passes
options.explanation: Modulation creates sidebands and can change the spectral result; a fixed test is insufficient.

options.text: No output equipment can respond to frequencies near the top of the band
options.explanation: The output chain may respond or introduce further nonlinear products; this is not a universal guarantee.

workedExample: The design accepts some folding in exchange for brightness. State the accepted band and test the whole table range, interpolation and intended modulation. Treat hearing and output-chain assumptions as conditions rather than relabelling the result alias-free.
